description: A full 78-card tarot deck reimagined through the lens of cricket. 22 Major Arcana of the game's rituals and turning points, plus 56 Minor Arcana across four suits: Bats (drive and ambition), Caps (feeling and belonging), Seam (mind and conflict), and Stumps (graft and results). Each suit traces a ten-step arc from a first spark through to a defining wicket, plus four court cards spanning rookie to master — every one of the 56 has its own standalone cricket name, not a generic rank label.

Bats.theme: drive, ambition, momentum, enterprise, attacking intent

Seam.theme: mind, strategy, conflict, hard truths, communication

Stumps.theme: graft, results, security, the body, the tangible

courts.The Colt: Page — the learner, the fresh prospect, curiosity and news
courts.The Quick: Knight — the mover, pursuit and momentum, action for better or worse
courts.The Senior Pro: Queen — mastery held inward, the dressing-room voice, leading by example
courts.The Great: King — mastery turned outward, command, authority and legacy

cards.name: The Debutant
cards.cricketMeaning: Walking out to bat or bowl for the very first time, cap on, heart pounding, everything still to prove.
cards.upright: A fresh start is here. Trust your instincts even though you haven't 'earned' the moment yet — everyone starts with a first over, a first innings. Take the guard and back yourself.
cards.reversed: Recklessness or hesitation at the crease. You're either charging in without a plan or too scared to leave the changing room. Find the middle ground before you play the shot.

cards.name: The Allrounder
cards.cricketMeaning: The player who can bat, bowl, and field with equal skill — turning whatever is at hand into a match-winning performance.
cards.upright: You have everything you need already. Skills, timing, and opportunity are aligning — it's time to contribute with bat and ball, not wait to be picked for one role.
cards.reversed: Spreading yourself too thin, or talent without application. A gifted player who never quite delivers. Focus on one skill and sharpen it.

cards.name: The Wicketkeeper
cards.cricketMeaning: Standing behind the stumps, saying little, seeing everything — the game's quiet intelligence.
cards.upright: Listen more than you speak. The answer you need isn't in noise or analysis — it's in the quiet read you already have on the situation. Trust the instinct behind the stumps.
cards.reversed: Ignoring your gut, or overthinking a simple appeal. You're second-guessing what you already know. Go back to instinct.

cards.name: The Home Ground
cards.cricketMeaning: A flat pitch, a friendly crowd, familiar conditions — everything set up for you to flourish.
cards.upright: Conditions favor you right now. Let yourself be supported, grow into the innings, and don't rush what's naturally building in your favor.
cards.reversed: Home comfort turning into complacency, or a supportive environment being taken for granted. Don't let easy conditions make you lazy.

cards.name: The Captain
cards.cricketMeaning: The one setting the field, making the calls, carrying the weight of every decision.
cards.upright: Step up and take control. A situation needs your structure and decisiveness — set the field, make the call, own the outcome.
cards.reversed: Over-control or rigid captaincy that stifles the team. You're micromanaging the field instead of trusting your bowlers. Loosen the grip.

cards.name: The Coach
cards.cricketMeaning: The voice in the nets reminding you of technique, discipline, and the basics that never go out of style.
cards.upright: Go back to fundamentals. A mentor, a coaching manual, or plain old discipline has the answer you're looking for. Respect the process.
cards.reversed: Blindly following outdated advice, or rejecting all guidance out of stubbornness. Question the method, but don't throw out the technique entirely.

cards.name: The Partnership
cards.cricketMeaning: Two batsmen at the crease, running on trust, building something neither could alone.
cards.upright: A relationship or collaboration is at a turning point — commit to it fully. Communicate clearly, run the singles, trust your partner.
cards.reversed: A breakdown in communication — a mix-up, a run-out waiting to happen. Miscommunication is the real danger here, not the opposition.

cards.name: The Chase
cards.cricketMeaning: Batting under lights, required run rate climbing, nothing but forward momentum and nerve.
cards.upright: Full steam ahead. You have the drive to pull this off — stay focused on the target and don't let doubt slow your running between the wickets.
cards.reversed: Losing control of the chase — panicking, changing plans mid-over, or trying to do too much too fast. Reset and rebuild the required rate calmly.

cards.name: The Anchor
cards.cricketMeaning: The batsman who holds one end steady through a collapse, absorbing pressure without flinching.
cards.upright: Real strength here is calm, not aggression. Hold your position, absorb the pressure, and let the storm around you pass without losing your composure.
cards.reversed: Forcing control through stubbornness, or crumbling under pressure you tried to just 'tough out.' Strength without patience becomes brittle.

cards.name: The Twelfth Man
cards.cricketMeaning: Watching from the boundary, drinks tray in hand, learning the game from the outside looking in.
cards.upright: Step back and observe before acting. This is a season for quiet reflection, not center stage — your moment will come, use this time to prepare.
cards.reversed: Isolating yourself when you should be engaging, or feeling permanently overlooked. Don't mistake being benched for being forgotten.

cards.name: The Toss
cards.cricketMeaning: The coin spinning in the air before a ball is bowled — fortune's first, unearned decision of the day.
cards.upright: Circumstances beyond your control are about to shift. A change of luck is coming — win or lose the toss, what matters is how you play the conditions you're given.
cards.reversed: A run of bad luck, or blaming fortune for outcomes you could still influence. The toss is only the start of the story, not the whole match.

cards.name: The Umpire
cards.cricketMeaning: The final word on every appeal — impartial, deliberate, bound by the laws of the game.
cards.upright: A fair and honest decision is needed, from you or about you. Trust the process, accept the outcome, and act with integrity even when it costs you.
cards.reversed: An unfair call, or refusing to accept a decision that's already been made. Dwelling on a bad decision only costs you the next ball.

cards.name: The Rain Delay
cards.cricketMeaning: Covers on, players off, the match suspended in limbo — nothing to do but wait and see it differently.
cards.upright: Progress is paused for a reason. Use this stoppage to see the situation from a new angle rather than fighting the delay. Sometimes waiting is the move.
cards.reversed: Resisting a necessary pause, or staying stuck in limbo long after play could resume. Don't let the delay become an excuse to stall.

cards.name: The Run Out
cards.cricketMeaning: Gone in an instant, no warning, no half-measures — one end of something, the start of another.
cards.upright: An abrupt ending is clearing space for what's next. Don't fight the finish — a chapter is closing so a new innings can begin.
cards.reversed: Refusing to accept something is over, dragging out an ending that's already happened. Walk off before you're given out.

cards.name: The Declaration
cards.cricketMeaning: The captain choosing exactly the right moment to stop batting — not too early, not too greedy.
cards.upright: Balance and good timing matter more than pushing for more. You have enough — declare, and set up the next phase from a position of strength.
cards.reversed: Bad timing — declaring too early out of impatience, or batting on too long out of greed. Reassess what 'enough' actually looks like.

cards.name: The Sledge
cards.cricketMeaning: Words from the slip cordon designed to get in your head — a test of what you'll let control you.
cards.upright: Something is baiting your ego — a rivalry, a grudge, a bad habit dressed up as competitive fire. Notice what's pulling your focus off the game.
cards.reversed: Breaking free from a temptation or toxic pattern that's had a grip on you. You're learning to let the sledging go unanswered.

cards.name: The Collapse
cards.cricketMeaning: Five wickets in five overs — the innings falling apart faster than anyone expected.
cards.upright: A sudden, disruptive event is dismantling something that looked stable. It's disorienting, but it's clearing out what wasn't built to last anyway.
cards.reversed: Fearing a collapse that hasn't happened yet, or narrowly avoiding one. Don't let anxiety about falling apart cost you the innings that's still in front of you.

cards.name: The Comeback
cards.cricketMeaning: Returning to the field after injury or a lean patch, quietly rebuilding form and belief.
cards.upright: Hope is well placed here. After a difficult stretch, healing and form are genuinely returning — trust the quiet signs of recovery.
cards.reversed: Losing faith just before the turnaround, or rushing the comeback before you're truly ready. Give the recovery the time it needs.

cards.name: The Floodlights
cards.cricketMeaning: A day-night match under lights and dew — the ball behaving strangely, nothing quite as it seems.
cards.upright: Things aren't fully clear right now, and that's okay. Move carefully through the uncertainty rather than assuming you can read conditions you can't yet see.
cards.reversed: Confusion lifting, or anxiety about the unknown that's bigger than the situation warrants. The dew will settle — don't panic-bowl at shadows.

cards.name: The Century
cards.cricketMeaning: Bat raised to the crowd, three figures on the board — pure, uncomplicated triumph.
cards.upright: Genuine success and joy are here, earned and deserved. Let yourself enjoy this moment fully — no caveats needed.
cards.reversed: Success that feels hollow, or joy you're not allowing yourself to feel. Don't undersell a century just because it wasn't a double.

cards.name: The Review
cards.cricketMeaning: Bat tucked under the arm, waiting on the big screen — a decision from the past being revisited and made right.
cards.upright: A past decision is being reconsidered, and you may get the reprieve you've been hoping for. Trust the review process and be honest about what really happened.
cards.reversed: Refusing to review your own mistakes, or burning a review on false hope. Be honest with yourself before you ask for a second look.

cards.name: The World Cup
cards.cricketMeaning: The trophy lifted, the long tournament finally complete — everything you worked for, whole and realized.
cards.upright: A long cycle is reaching genuine completion. Whatever you've been building toward has arrived — take it in before starting the next campaign.
cards.reversed: Something close to completion but not quite there — a final short of the boundary. Don't stop chasing just before the finish line.

cards.name: The Middle
cards.cricketMeaning: The ball comes off the middle of the bat on the very first ball faced — no fuss, no doubt, pure connection.
cards.upright: Something is about to connect clean and true. Trust the shot you're already shaping up to play — the timing is right, so commit fully instead of checking your grip.
cards.reversed: All backlift, no follow-through — you're set up to swing but flinching at the last second. Stop adjusting your stance and play the ball that's actually coming.

cards.name: The Quick Call
cards.cricketMeaning: One batter calls, the other has a split second to trust it and go — hesitate and you're both stranded mid-pitch.
cards.upright: A decision needs two people fully committed, right now, not half-committed while they wait and see. Call it clearly, and trust whoever's backing you up to move the second you do.
cards.reversed: Mixed signals, a call sent too late, two people running for the same ground. Stop assuming the other person heard you — say it again, louder, before someone gets run out.

cards.name: The Scramble
cards.cricketMeaning: A misfield in the deep and two batters who were only ever going for two suddenly sprint a third, purely on effort.
cards.upright: Someone else's stumble just opened a door you didn't plan for. Don't stand there admiring it — put your head down and take the extra ground while it's there.
cards.reversed: Greed for one run too many, and you're the one left short of your ground. Know the difference between a real opportunity and you just wanting more than what's on offer.

cards.name: The Cover Drive
cards.cricketMeaning: Front foot, full extension, the ball placed exactly where three fielders weren't standing — no risk, no luck, just a shot played properly.
cards.upright: You already know how to do this well — it's less about a burst of brilliance and more about trusting the technique you've built. Play it straight, play it controlled, and let the result take care of itself.
cards.reversed: Trying to force elegance into a situation that actually needs you to scrap and survive. Not every ball is a cover-drive ball — sometimes the ugly block is the right shot.

cards.name: The Overthrow
cards.cricketMeaning: A clean stop turns into a wild throw that beats every fielder backing up — suddenly two easy runs are four, and nobody quite meant for that to happen.
cards.upright: Things are about to get messier and faster than anyone planned, for better or worse. Stay alert rather than relaxed — a situation already moving can swing further than you expect.
cards.reversed: The panic after the mistake is doing more damage than the mistake itself. Stop chasing the ball all over the ground — pick it up cleanly and reset, one throw at a time.

cards.name: The Maximum
cards.cricketMeaning: Middled, timed, and gone — over the rope before the fielder's even turned around, the biggest result available off a single ball.
cards.upright: This is a moment to go big rather than nudge safely into a gap. You've read this one right — commit fully and take the maximum on offer.
cards.reversed: Swinging for the fences on a ball that only ever needed a single. Ambition's outrun the actual situation — scale it back before you lose your wicket chasing a bigger result than was ever required.

cards.name: The Inside Edge
cards.cricketMeaning: The ball beats the bat, clips the inside edge, and rolls just wide of the stumps — you're still in, but only just, and you both know it.
cards.upright: You got away with something, and that's worth noticing rather than ignoring. Use the reprieve to actually adjust what you're doing, not just to relax and assume your luck holds.
cards.reversed: Mistaking a lucky survival for a plan that's working. The edges are starting to add up — go back to basics before the next one doesn't miss the stumps.

cards.name: The Charge
cards.cricketMeaning: Feet moving before the ball's even left the bowler's hand, closing the gap to turn a good length ball into a bad one.
cards.upright: Waiting for the perfect moment has stopped being useful — it's time to move toward what you want instead of hoping it comes to you. Commit to the charge; half-measures get you stumped.
cards.reversed: Charging at something that was never actually there, caught stranded out of your ground. Read the situation properly before you commit your whole body to it — this one wasn't worth the risk.

cards.name: The Heavy Legs
cards.cricketMeaning: Late in a long innings, every run between the wickets feels like wading through wet sand, but the bat's still in your hands and the stumps are still standing.
cards.upright: You're allowed to be exhausted and still keep going — the two aren't opposites. Find one more effort rather than a final burst; steady beats spectacular from here.
cards.reversed: Running on empty and refusing to admit it, one mistimed step from a real injury. This is the moment to ask for the physio or the runner, not to grind through on pride alone.

cards.name: The Fatal Charge
cards.cricketMeaning: The same charge that's worked all innings finally meets a ball it can't reach — stumped by a yard, the bold approach finally catching up with itself.
cards.upright: The approach that got you this far is reaching its natural limit — not because it was wrong, but because every streak has an end written into it. Recognize when the story wants to close rather than forcing one more chapter.
cards.reversed: Refusing to accept that this particular run is over, trying to relive the same charge past its use-by date. Let this version end cleanly so the next one can start fresh, instead of dragging a good thing past where it wanted to stop.

cards.name: The Net Basher
cards.cricketMeaning: First one at the nets, last one to leave, smashing throwdowns with more heart than technique and grinning through every mishit.
cards.upright: An exciting new spark of ambition has arrived, still rough round the edges — don't polish it into caution too early. Let the enthusiasm actually run for a while before you start correcting the technique.
cards.reversed: All big talk about what you're going to do, none of it actually happening at the crease. Stop rehearsing the shot in your head and go hit an actual ball.

cards.name: The Pinch Hitter
cards.cricketMeaning: Promoted up the order for one job only — get after it fast, before the bowlers have found their length or the fielders their positions.
cards.upright: You've been put in this position because someone trusts your instincts more than a slow build-up right now. Go hard early — the advantage is in speed, not patience.
cards.reversed: Swinging wildly because you were told to attack, without actually reading what's needed. Boldness without a plan is just recklessness wearing a brave face — pick your ball.

cards.name: The Finisher
cards.cricketMeaning: Unbeaten at the other end while wickets fall around them, quietly farming the strike and doing the arithmetic nobody else has the head for right now.
cards.upright: You don't need to be the loudest person in the room to be the one actually steering it home. Trust the quiet, practiced calm you've built — it's exactly what this moment needs.
cards.reversed: Carrying the whole finish alone because you don't trust anyone else to share the load. Let someone else take strike for an over — you don't have to close every single gap yourself.

cards.name: The Match-Winner
cards.cricketMeaning: One player, on one afternoon, simply better than the game around them — every risk lands, every gap gets found, the result never really in doubt once they got going.
cards.upright: You have real, earned command over this situation — stop second-guessing it. This is the moment to back your own judgment completely and let your ability decide the outcome.
cards.reversed: Mistaking one big moment for permanent authority, coasting on reputation instead of doing the work again. Past brilliance doesn't bat for you today — you still have to show up and earn this one too.

cards.name: The Warm Welcome
cards.cricketMeaning: Walking into a new dressing room for the first time and finding your kit bag already has a peg with your name on it.
cards.upright: You're being welcomed into something warmly and genuinely — let yourself actually accept it instead of standing awkwardly by the door. Belonging doesn't have to be earned before it's offered.
cards.reversed: A welcome that feels a little too smooth, or one you can't quite let yourself believe. Give it time before deciding whether the warmth is real or just politeness.

cards.name: The Handshake at Tea
cards.cricketMeaning: Two players who spent the whole session trying to get each other out, shaking hands over sandwiches like none of it was personal — because it wasn't.
cards.upright: There's real warmth available here if you're willing to set the competition down for a moment. A sincere gesture right now will land better than you expect.
cards.reversed: Going through the motions of friendliness while still keeping score underneath. Notice if the handshake is genuine or just for show before you decide how much to trust it.

cards.name: The Team Huddle
cards.cricketMeaning: Eleven players in a tight circle before the first ball, one voice saying what needs saying and ten more nodding along with it.
cards.upright: You don't have to carry this alone — the people around you are already leaning in, ready to help. Let the group hold some of the weight instead of insisting on doing it solo.
cards.reversed: A huddle that's more noise than substance, everyone talking and nobody actually listening. Real support needs real honesty in the circle, not just performed enthusiasm.

cards.name: The Flat Net Session
cards.cricketMeaning: An hour in the nets that technically happened — balls bowled, shots played, nobody actually present in any of it.
cards.upright: Something that should matter to you is starting to feel like a chore, and that's worth noticing before it becomes a habit. A small, deliberate act of actually caring again will do more than forcing more effort.
cards.reversed: Waking up out of the flatness and realizing how disengaged you'd become. Good — now actually do something different with it instead of just feeling bad about the last few weeks.

cards.name: The Dropped Catch
cards.cricketMeaning: Sitter of a catch, straight into the hands, straight back out again — the whole ground goes quiet for a second in sympathy.
cards.upright: Something genuinely slipped through your hands, and it's fair to feel that. Just don't stand there staring at your palms so long that you miss the next chance that's already coming.
cards.reversed: Still replaying the drop a dozen overs later, letting one mistake define the whole day. It's already gone — put it down properly and get back in position for the next one.

cards.name: The Backyard Game
cards.cricketMeaning: Tennis ball, a rubbish bin for stumps, someone's little brother fielding at deep everything — the exact moment most of them fell in love with this game.
cards.upright: Something warm from simpler days is worth revisiting right now, not as an escape but as a reminder of why any of this matters. Let that old joy back in.
cards.reversed: Living so far back in the good old days that you can't actually enjoy the game in front of you. Honour the memory, then come back to the innings you're actually playing today.

cards.name: The Daydream
cards.cricketMeaning: Standing at the non-striker's end picturing the century speech instead of watching the bowler's run-up — three overs and two dropped concentration later, it shows.
cards.upright: There are a lot of appealing versions of how this could go, and that's exactly the trap — pick one and commit instead of admiring all of them at once. Clarity beats options here.
cards.reversed: Caught completely flat-footed because you were somewhere else in your head. Come back to the actual ball being bowled at you right now — the daydream isn't going to bat for you.

cards.name: The Long Walk Back
cards.cricketMeaning: Bat under the arm, helmet off, walking off a ground that used to feel like everything — not in defeat, just done with what it used to mean.
cards.upright: Something you've outgrown is asking to be left behind, even if it once mattered enormously. It's okay to walk toward something quieter and more honest than where you've been standing.
cards.reversed: Staying in a situation purely out of habit or fear of what leaving might mean. The walk back doesn't have to be dramatic — it just has to actually happen when you're ready.

cards.name: The Man of the Match
cards.cricketMeaning: Name called out over the tannoy, a small trophy that won't mean much to anyone else, and a feeling in your chest that this one actually counted.
cards.upright: Something you genuinely worked for has landed, and it's allowed to feel as good as it does. Don't rush past this moment looking for the next thing to worry about.
cards.reversed: Success that should feel satisfying but somehow doesn't, like the trophy's for someone else's effort. Figure out what's actually missing before you write off something you worked hard for.

cards.name: The Team Photo
cards.cricketMeaning: Trophy in the middle, arms slung over shoulders, everyone in shot for once — the individual scores stop mattering the second the camera clicks.
cards.upright: This is a genuinely harmonious moment, built by everyone around you as much as by you. Let yourself be fully present in it instead of already thinking about what comes next.
cards.reversed: Standing in the photo but feeling apart from it, like the closeness on show isn't quite the closeness you actually feel. Say something honest to the people in that frame before the distance grows.

cards.name: The New Recruit
cards.cricketMeaning: First training session with a new team, still learning everyone's names, already desperate to be liked and to earn a place in the group.
cards.upright: Someone or something new is approaching you with real openness — meet it the same way instead of guarding yourself. Fresh enthusiasm deserves a genuine welcome, not suspicion.
cards.reversed: Trying so hard to be liked that you're not actually being yourself around the new group. Let them see the real version — that's who they'll actually want to keep around.

cards.name: The Enforcer
cards.cricketMeaning: The moment a teammate gets sledged too hard and someone else in the field walks straight over, jaw set, before the umpire's even noticed.
cards.upright: Someone you care about needs you to step in right now, not think it over for a week. Let the loyalty move you — this isn't the moment for careful neutrality.
cards.reversed: Fighting someone else's battle so hard you've made it about you instead of them. Check whether you're actually helping, or just enjoying being the one who steps in.

cards.name: The Dressing Room Glue
cards.cricketMeaning: Not the biggest name on the team sheet, but the one every single player goes to first — before the coach, before the captain — when something's actually wrong.
cards.upright: You have real influence here, built on trust rather than title. Use it to hold the people around you together — that quiet role matters more than the scoreboard shows.
cards.reversed: Holding everyone else together while nobody's checking in on you. It's fine to need someone to be the glue for you occasionally — ask, rather than waiting to be noticed.

cards.name: The Captain's Captain
cards.cricketMeaning: The rival captain who, after a brutal loss, is still the first person everyone wants leading them — respected as much by opponents as by their own side.
cards.upright: The respect you've built runs deeper than the current result, and you can lean on that. Lead from that trust rather than needing to prove anything further.
cards.reversed: Coasting on a reputation for being respected instead of still actually earning it day to day. That standing was built through consistent care — it needs tending, not just remembering.

cards.name: The Perfect Line
cards.cricketMeaning: A ball that lands on exactly the spot it needed to, nagging just outside off stump, and the batter suddenly has no good option at all.
cards.upright: A clear, precise read on the situation has just arrived — trust it completely rather than second-guessing something that finally makes sense. Act while the clarity's still sharp.
cards.reversed: Overthinking a plan that was already working, changing the line for no real reason. Go back to the read you trusted five minutes ago — you didn't need to fix it.

cards.name: The Leave
cards.cricketMeaning: Bat lifted high, ball let through to the keeper untouched — not a mistake, exactly, but not a decision either, just two sides waiting each other out.
cards.upright: Sometimes the strongest move is genuinely not playing a shot yet. Hold your position calmly instead of forcing a decision the situation isn't actually asking for.
cards.reversed: Leaving so many balls that you've stopped scoring at all, indecision dressed up as discipline. At some point not choosing becomes its own kind of losing — pick a line and commit.

cards.name: The Nick Behind
keywords: the edge you can't take back
cards.cricketMeaning: The faintest brush of bat on ball, gone before you've even registered the sound, and the umpire's finger is already going up.
cards.upright: A hard truth just landed, sudden and undeniable — there's no reviewing this one, so don't waste energy arguing with it. Accept it clean and walk off with your head up.
cards.reversed: Standing your ground on something everyone else already knows is true. The longer you wait for the decision to change, the worse the walk off is going to look.

cards.name: The Drinks Break
cards.cricketMeaning: Twelfth man jogging out with a tray of bottles and a towel, both sides taking sixty seconds to just stand still and breathe.
cards.upright: You're allowed to actually stop for a moment instead of playing through. A short, deliberate pause now will serve the next session far better than pushing straight through it.
cards.reversed: Using the break to spiral about what's already happened instead of actually resting. This pause is for recovery, not rehearsing the worry — put the thoughts down along with the bottle.

cards.name: The Run Rate Battle
cards.cricketMeaning: Required rate climbing every over, both sides doing the same math in their heads, the game turning into arithmetic as much as cricket.
cards.upright: This situation has turned into a genuine contest, and pretending otherwise won't help. Face the numbers directly and compete for it — the pressure is real, but so is your ability to answer it.
cards.reversed: Getting so fixated on the equation that you've stopped playing the actual ball in front of you. Step back from the run rate for one moment and just play what's bowled.

cards.name: The New Ball
cards.cricketMeaning: Eighty overs of grinding wear suddenly gone — a fresh, hard ball in hand and the whole contest tilts to a different kind of fight.
cards.upright: Whatever's been building is about to shift into a genuinely new phase. Meet the change with fresh energy rather than dragging the old approach into conditions that have already moved on.
cards.reversed: Still playing by the rules of a situation that's already changed underneath you. Notice the reset that's happened and adjust, instead of getting caught out by conditions you haven't clocked yet.

cards.name: The Slower Ball
cards.cricketMeaning: Same arm speed, same run-up, completely different pace off the pitch — the shot's already committed before the batter realizes they've been had.
cards.upright: Not everything needs to be delivered at full pace to land well. A little misdirection or patience, used honestly, can get you further than forcing the obvious approach.
cards.reversed: Being on the receiving end of someone else's deception, or catching yourself trying to pull one over on people who trust you. Either way, it's time to call it what it is.

cards.name: The Maiden Over
cards.cricketMeaning: Six balls, not a run scored, the field creeping in a fraction with every dot — nothing dramatic happening, and that's exactly the point.
cards.upright: You're in a holding pattern right now, and it's tighter than it looks from outside. Stay patient and disciplined rather than forcing an escape — the pressure you're building is doing real work.
cards.reversed: Feeling trapped by restrictions that are actually mostly self-imposed at this point. Look honestly at what's really boxing you in before assuming there's no way to score off this bowling.

cards.name: The Sleepless Night Before
cards.cricketMeaning: Staring at the ceiling the night before a big match, replaying deliveries that haven't happened yet against batters who aren't even out there.
cards.upright: The worry is bigger right now than the actual situation warrants — that's just how the night before big things tends to feel. Get through the night as best you can; the morning will be more manageable than this feels.
cards.reversed: Letting the anxious spiral cost you sleep for something that's still days away, or long since over. Name what's actually keeping you up, out loud, to someone — it loses power once it's said.

cards.name: The Broken Stumps
cards.cricketMeaning: Ball crashes clean through and the stumps go flying — no review, no argument, no ambiguity left in the situation at all.
cards.upright: Something is ending completely and unarguably, and as painful as that is, there's a real relief underneath it. There's nothing left to negotiate — let this one be fully, finally over.
cards.reversed: Trying to piece something back together that's actually, genuinely finished. Picking up the broken stumps and propping them back up won't undo what's already happened — it's time to walk off.

cards.name: The Apprentice Spinner
cards.cricketMeaning: Bowling in the nets with three different grips taped to memory, most of them still landing a foot off where they're meant to.
cards.upright: You're still learning the finer points of something, and that's exactly as it should be right now. Keep experimenting openly rather than expecting mastery before you've earned it.
cards.reversed: Trying to bowl the googly before you've got the stock ball under control. Get the basics reliable first — the clever tricks will actually work once the foundation's solid.

cards.name: The Strike Bowler
cards.cricketMeaning: Fifth over of a fresh spell, still steaming in at full pace, refusing to let the batter settle into anything comfortable.
cards.upright: Keep pressing — the breakthrough you're after comes from sustained intent, not a single lucky ball. Stay aggressive and trust that persistence is doing more than it looks like from here.
cards.reversed: Running in hard over after over for a wicket that isn't coming, wearing yourself down chasing something that needs a change of plan, not more effort in the same direction.

cards.name: The Analyst
cards.cricketMeaning: Sitting quietly in the changing room with a notebook, spotting the exact half-second hesitation in the batter's trigger movement nobody else has clocked.
cards.upright: You already see the pattern that matters here, even if you haven't said it out loud yet. Trust the quiet observation you've made and share it — it's more useful than it feels.
cards.reversed: Overanalyzing a situation until the simple, obvious read gets buried under seventeen layers of theory. Sometimes the first thing you noticed was the right one — stop looking for a cleverer answer.

cards.name: The Bowling Captain
cards.cricketMeaning: Field set to the inch, bowling changes called two overs before anyone else sees why, the whole shape of the contest bending around one person's plan.
cards.upright: You have real command of the strategic picture here — trust your read and set the terms rather than reacting to someone else's plan. This is your situation to shape.
cards.reversed: Micromanaging every detail because you don't trust the plan to hold without you controlling it directly. Set the field, then let your bowlers actually bowl — the plan doesn't need you gripping it this tightly.

cards.name: The Contract Offer
cards.cricketMeaning: An envelope with a new club's letterhead, terms attached, a real and specific chance sitting there waiting on a signature.
cards.upright: A concrete, practical opportunity is genuinely available to you right now — not a maybe, an actual offer. Take it seriously enough to actually read the fine print and consider saying yes.
cards.reversed: An opportunity that looks solid on paper but has something off in the details. Don't sign anything, literally or figuratively, until you've actually checked what you're agreeing to.

cards.name: The Balancing Act
cards.cricketMeaning: Training in the morning, a day job in the afternoon, and somehow still turning up fresh enough to bat well on the weekend.
cards.upright: You're juggling more than one real priority right now, and that's manageable if you stay deliberate about it. Keep both plates spinning with attention rather than letting either one drop from neglect.
cards.reversed: Dropping one responsibility to barely hold the other, the balance actually failing rather than just looking difficult. Something has to genuinely give here — decide which, rather than letting exhaustion decide for you.

cards.name: The Fielding Drill
cards.cricketMeaning: An hour of throw-downs and diving practice with the rest of the fielding unit, everyone's individual effort adding up to something sharper than any one of them alone.
cards.upright: What you're building right now works because other people are building it with you. Let the collaboration actually count instead of measuring only your own individual contribution.
cards.reversed: Doing all the unglamorous work while someone else gets credited for the sharp fielding. Say something about it plainly, rather than quietly resenting a team effort that wasn't recognized fairly.

cards.name: The Defensive Block
cards.cricketMeaning: Full stride forward, bat and pad together, the ball meeting dead wood and dropping harmlessly at your feet — nothing gained, but nothing lost either.
cards.upright: This is a moment to protect what you've already got rather than chase more. A tight, controlled hold on your position is the right move, even if it isn't exciting.
cards.reversed: Gripping so tightly to security that you've stopped scoring anything at all. Protecting what you have has value, but not if it costs you every chance to actually build on it.

cards.name: The Injury List
cards.cricketMeaning: Kit packed away in a locker, watching from the viewing area with a strapped-up wrist, while the team you'd normally be part of gets on with it without you.
cards.upright: Something's kept you out of a situation you'd normally be right in the middle of, and that's a genuine loss worth acknowledging. Use the enforced pause to actually heal rather than fighting to get back before you're ready.
cards.reversed: Coming back before you're properly recovered, trading a longer setback for a shorter one out of impatience. The list exists to protect you — don't argue your way off it too early.

cards.name: The Benefit Match
cards.cricketMeaning: A whole ground turning out on a Sunday for a veteran nobody's paying to watch, gate money going straight to the player who gave the club two decades.
cards.upright: There's real generosity available here, in both directions — give what you can and let yourself receive what's offered without deflecting it. This kind of sharing strengthens everyone involved.
cards.reversed: Generosity that comes with strings attached, or a gift you feel obligated rather than genuinely willing to accept. Check whether the giving here is actually free, or a debt being quietly created.

cards.name: The Long Rebuild
cards.cricketMeaning: A team stripped back after a bad season, blooding young players in front of empty stands, betting on a result that's still three years away.
cards.upright: This isn't going to pay off quickly, and that's fine — you're building something that needs time, not a shortcut. Stay patient with the slow, unglamorous work; it's genuinely adding up.
cards.reversed: Losing faith in a long process right before it starts to turn, or refusing to actually invest the patience it needs. Check whether you're really out of time, or just out of patience.

cards.name: The Thousand Throwdowns
cards.cricketMeaning: Same shot, same length, ball after ball after ball, a bucket refilled a dozen times before anyone's watching or clapping for any of it.
cards.upright: The unglamorous, repeated effort you're putting in is genuinely building something real, even without an audience. Keep grinding at the fundamentals — this is exactly how mastery actually gets made.
cards.reversed: Mistaking sheer volume of effort for the right kind of effort, grinding at a flaw without actually fixing it. Get someone to actually watch and correct you before you groove the mistake in deeper.

cards.name: The Testimonial Year
cards.cricketMeaning: One final season given entirely in your honour, no pressure attached, just a chance to enjoy the game on your own terms after years of grinding for everyone else.
cards.upright: You've earned the right to a little ease here — this isn't laziness, it's a season you built for yourself through years of work. Let yourself enjoy it without guilt.
cards.reversed: Comfortable enough now that you've stopped pushing at all, coasting on past effort rather than staying genuinely engaged. Earned ease is still meant to be lived in, not just sat on.

cards.name: The Retired Number
cards.cricketMeaning: A shirt with your number on it, framed and hung in the pavilion, still there for players who weren't even born when you were playing.
cards.upright: What you're building here has the potential to genuinely outlast you — think beyond the current result to what it leaves behind. That long-term legacy is worth investing in deliberately.
cards.reversed: Chasing a legacy so hard you've stopped being present in the actual work that would create one. The number gets retired because of what you did while playing, not because you wanted it retired.

cards.name: The Academy Grinder
cards.cricketMeaning: First one at the ground for pre-dawn fitness, doing the extra sprints nobody's making them do, still years from a first-team game.
cards.upright: Nobody's watching this early effort yet, and that's exactly why it matters — it's building the foundation everything else will stand on. Keep showing up for the unglamorous hours.
cards.reversed: Grinding so hard, so early, that burnout is creeping in before the career's even properly started. Even foundational work needs rest built into it — this isn't sustainable at this pace.

cards.name: The Diving Fielder
keywords: throwing your body on the line
cards.cricketMeaning: Full stretch in the deep, boots leaving the turf, saving a run that most fielders would've let go — the kind of effort that doesn't show up in any stat.
cards.upright: This is a moment for full physical commitment rather than careful calculation. Throw yourself at it — the effort itself is the point, whether or not you actually get there.
cards.reversed: Diving for things that were never really catchable, risking your body for marginal gains. Pick your moments to go all-in — not every ball needs a full-length dive.

cards.name: The Physio
cards.cricketMeaning: The person every player quietly goes to first, taping ankles and talking players through niggles before anyone tells the coach there's a problem.
cards.upright: You have real, practical mastery in keeping things — and people — in working order, even if it happens quietly and off the scoreboard. Trust that steady, hands-on care; it matters more than it's credited for.
cards.reversed: So busy keeping everyone else in working order that your own maintenance has slipped. Book yourself in too — the person who fixes everyone else still needs fixing sometimes.

cards.name: The Century Machine
cards.cricketMeaning: A name that goes into the team sheet in pen, not pencil, because the runs simply keep coming, series after series, without much needing to be said about it.
cards.upright: Your track record has earned you real standing here — let the consistent results speak instead of over-explaining or justifying yourself. Quiet, repeated output is its own authority.
cards.reversed: Leaning entirely on a reputation for consistency while the actual output has started slipping. The name in pen still needs the runs behind it — don't let the past record write checks the present can't cash.
